overview.title: Overview
overview.desc: The Wildcat Chat Overlay displays Twitch and YouTube Live chat messages inside OBS Studio. You can configure settings in the Chat Scene Creator on the web or directly inside the OBS browser source.
overview.getStarted: Get Started with the Chat Overlay →

platforms.title: Platform Support
platforms.desc: The chat overlay connects to various streaming platforms. You can configure your target platform from within the configuration panel in OBS.
platforms.twitch: Twitch: Enter your channel name (for example, `wildcatgamer`). Badges and emotes are natively supported.
platforms.youtube: YouTube: Supports YouTube live chat for both public and unlisted streams. For public streams, enter your channel username, channel ID, video URL, or video ID. For unlisted streams, the video URL is required. (Note: Private streams are not supported).

customization.title: Customization & Themes
customization.desc: The chat overlay includes powerful aesthetic customization tools. You can change fundamental styling directly through the config menu.

obsConfig.title: Configuration Options: You can configure chat settings in two ways:
obsConfig.step1: Web Chat Scene Creator (Recommended): Configure channel connections, fonts, themes, colors, and layouts on the web. Enable Live Sync to stream edits live to OBS.
obsConfig.step2: In OBS Settings Panel: Right-click the Browser Source in OBS and select Interact. Hover over the chat and click the settings gear () to customize settings locally.
obsConfig.step3: Settings save automatically for each scene source.

themes.title: Automatic AI Themes
themes.desc: One of the most powerful features of the Wildcat Chat Overlay is its natural-language AI theme generator. Inside the config panel, simply type a description of the vibe, mood, or aesthetic you want (for example, "cyberpunk neon night," "cozy wooden cabin in the snow," "vintage 90s vaporwave"). The overlay will intelligently generate the corresponding CSS variables, adjust the color palettes for ideal contrast, and apply the theme live!

emotes.title: Third-Party Emotes & Stacking
emotes.desc: The Wildcat Chat Overlay natively supports third-party Twitch emote providers, including BetterTTV (BTTV), FrankerFaceZ (FFZ), and 7TV. Both global and channel-specific emote sets are loaded automatically for Twitch channels.

zeroWidth.title: Zero-Width & Overlay Stacking
zeroWidth.desc: Zero-width emotes (such as hats, masks, rain effects, or seasonal overlays) dynamically stack on top of the preceding emote when separated by a space (for example catJAM cvHazmat). Consecutive zero-width emotes can chain to create complex multi-layered emote stacks. Single-emote enlargement automatically applies to stacked emote combinations.

precedence.title: Priority & Matching
precedence.desc: Emotes are matched as exact, case-sensitive words. Twitch native emotes take priority over third-party emotes, and channel emotes take priority over global sets.

safety.title: Content Safety & Customization
safety.desc: You can fine-tune third-party emote behavior directly in the settings panel:
safety.toggle: Third-Party Emotes Toggle: Master switch to enable or disable all third-party emotes (enabled by default).
safety.channelToggle: Show Channel Emotes: Toggle whether channel-specific third-party emotes are displayed or restricted to global sets only.
safety.filters: 7TV Safety Filters: Filter out potentially sensitive or unwanted emotes by category, including Twitch Disallowed (filtered by default), Sexual Content, Epilepsy / Flashing, and Edgy / Offensive.

config.title: Config Panel Features
config.desc: All of the modifications and customizations are handled directly using the on-page settings menu. In OBS, right-click the Browser Source and select Interact to open the menu. The options include:
config.feature1: Channel Selection: Select the streaming platform (Twitch/YouTube) and provide the relevant Channel ID or Video URL to connect.
config.feature2: Font Settings: Choose from an array of included Google Fonts and adjust the font size up to the maximum constraints, ensuring ideal readability.
config.feature3: Display Layout: Pick between standard list mode or popup chat bubbles mode. Adjust background opacities and borders.
config.feature4: Badges & Emotes: Toggle platform badges natively for Twitch and YouTube, and configure third-party emotes (BTTV, FFZ, 7TV), zero-width stacking, and content safety filters.
config.feature5: Theme Management: Access your AI-generated Themes, select from presets, and adjust granular colors manually if needed.

scenes.title: Chat Scene Creator
scenes.desc: The Chat Scene Creator lets you create and manage chat scenes for different parts of your stream (for example, Gaming or Just Chatting).
scenes.feature1: Scene Management: Create, duplicate, delete, import, and export scene settings files in JSON format.
scenes.feature2: Visual Web Customization: Set Twitch and YouTube channel connections, Google Fonts, preset themes, AI-generated themes, colors, background opacity, chroma key green screen mode, popup layout, platform badges, and third-party emotes.
scenes.feature3: Live Preview: Test settings live in an interactive preview window before streaming.
scenes.syncDesc: When you enable Web Customization (Live Sync), the Chat Scene Creator creates a unique sync token and includes it in your OBS URL: chat.html?scene=NAME&sync=TOKEN. Edits saved in the web UI update your OBS browser source live in real time without refreshing the page.
scenes.localNote: If Live Sync is disabled, settings save locally in your browser or in the OBS browser source cache.

obsSetup.title: OBS Setup Instructions
obsSetup.desc: Follow these steps to add the chat overlay to OBS Studio:
obsSetup.step1: In OBS Studio, go to the Sources panel, click the + button, and select Browser.
obsSetup.step2: Enter a recognizable source name (for example, "Twitch Chat").
obsSetup.step3: Paste the URL generated from the Chat Scene Creator into the URL field. Uncheck "Local file" if you cannot paste the URL.
obsSetup.step4: Set Width to 320 and Height to 600.
obsSetup.step5: Click "OK" to add the browser source to your overlay canvas.
obsSetup.step6: Configuring Settings: If Live Sync is enabled, save your settings in the Web Chat Scene Creator. If Live Sync is disabled, right-click the Browser Source in OBS and select Interact to open the settings panel.
obsSetup.step7: In the interactive window, enter your channel information, select your preferences by clicking the gear icon () on the top-right, and click "Connect".

tips.title: Advanced OBS Tips
tips.tip1: Enable Shutdown source when not visible to save CPU/Memory overhead.
tips.tip2: To hide any scrollbars, add body { overflow: hidden; } to the Custom CSS field inside the properties window.
tips.tip3: Settings are saved to OBS cache. If you ever "Clear Cache" in OBS for this source, you will need to reconfigure the aesthetic settings.

colors.title: Color Customization
colors.desc: You have full control over the color of every element in the chat overlay. Since standard color picker dialogs don't work inside the OBS browser source, all colors are set by entering hex codes directly (e.g. #FF5500). Each color setting also provides preset buttons with dynamic color swatches so you can see your current scheme at a glance.
colors.tip: Tip: You can search Google for "color picker" to use a built-in interactive color picker tool, then copy and paste the resulting hex codes directly into the settings fields.

available.title: Available Color Settings
available.bg: Background Color: The main background of chat messages. Works together with the background opacity slider for transparency control.
available.border: Border Color: The border around chat message bubbles.
available.text: Text Color: The color of chat message text.
available.username: Username Color: The color of usernames displayed next to messages. You can also enable Override Username Colors to use your custom color instead of each user's Twitch name color.
available.timestamp: Timestamp Color: The color of message timestamps (when timestamps are enabled).
available.pronoun: Pronoun Badge Color: The color of pronoun badges displayed next to usernames (when pronouns are enabled). This can also be set to automatically match the timestamp color.

animations.title: Animations
animations.desc: Chat message entry and exit animations use the Web Animations API for smooth, performant transitions. In window mode, new messages glide into view using a CSS clipping-based offset animation on the entire message list, avoiding per-element height animations that can cause jitter during busy chat. In popup mode, messages animate in and out with height and opacity transitions.

reducedMotion.title: Reduced Motion Support
reducedMotion.desc: The overlay respects the system-level prefers-reduced-motion setting (e.g. the "Reduce motion" option in macOS Accessibility settings). When enabled, entry animations are disabled for window-mode messages and popup transition durations are minimized, providing a calmer viewing experience.
